question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.35$ | $0.25$ |

If $\text{E}[X]=3.2$ and $\text{E}[Y]=3.8,$ calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$

current_example.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.4$ | $0.2$ |

If $\textrm{E} [X]=2.8$ and $\textrm{E}[Y] = 2.4,$ calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The covariance of $X$ and $Y$ can be calculated using the formula

$$
\textrm{Cov}[X,Y]
=
\textrm{E} [XY] - \textrm{E}[X]\cdot \textrm{E}[Y].
$$

We use the rule of the lazy statistician to find $\textrm{E}[XY]\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}xy\cdot f(x,y) \\  & =(1)(2)(0.2)+(1)(3)(0.2)+(4)(2)(0.4)+(4)(3)(0.2) \\  & =6.6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =6.6-(2.8)(2.4) \\  & =-0.12.\end{aligned}
$$
